title: A warning that advertises theft
hook: What does a theft warning imply about what other visitors do?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Contrast a descriptive norm about misconduct with an injunction against it.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Contrast a descriptive norm about misconduct with an injunction against it.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: Two illustrative sign conditions have theft rates 7.9% and 1.7%. What is their absolute gap? Toy inputs A=[7.9, 1.7]; B=[1.7, 1.7].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[7.9, 1.7, 6.2], [1.7, 1.7, 0]]. Labels: Descriptive %, Injunctive %, Gap pp.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: The two sign types can convey different messages about what others do and what is approved. The calculation compares the supplied rates; it does not establish that every warning will increase theft or transport this effect to another setting.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Descriptive %=1.7, Injunctive %=1.7. What is Gap pp? Answer: 0.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Descriptive %=1.7, Injunctive %=1.7. What is Gap pp?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 0. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: A sign at Petrified Forest saying many visitors stole wood raised theft to 7.9%, versus 1.7% for a sign simply asking people not to take it (Cialdini, 2003).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Contrast a descriptive norm about misconduct with an injunction against it.
